title: Corporate Travel Programmes: Service Level and Account Management Schedule
content:
Ten hours a day at one end of the range and around the clock at the other: the service desk hours, the first-response target, the service credit, the account management arrangements and the training allowance of the Corporate Travel Programmes are all graded by tier, and this schedule publishes them.

| Programme tier | Desk staffed (hours a day) | First-response target (minutes) | Service credit on a missed target (per cent of the monthly subscription) | Named account manager | Quarterly business review | Training sessions each contract year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business Starter Programme | 10 | 480 | 0 | No | No | 0 |
| Business Team Programme | 12 | 240 | 0 | No | No | 1 |
| Business Pro Programme | 16 | 120 | 5 | No | No | 2 |
| Business Enterprise Programme | 24 | 60 | 10 | Yes | Yes | 4 |
| Business Enterprise Plus Programme | 24 | 30 | 15 | Yes | Yes | 8 |
| Business Global Programme | 24 | 15 | 20 | Yes | Yes | 12 |

What the columns state: the hours a day the programme's service desk is staffed; the minutes within which the service desk targets a first response; the percentage of the monthly subscription credited when the response target is missed; whether a named account manager is assigned to the programme; whether a formal quarterly business review is held with the company; and the training sessions for the company's travellers included each contract year.

Three tiers are staffed for 24 hours a day, and they are distinguished from one another by their response targets of 60, 30 and 15 minutes and by service credits of 10, 15 and 20 per cent. The two lowest tiers publish a service credit of 0 per cent, and the Business Starter Programme publishes 0 training sessions each contract year; both are published figures for those tiers.
